title: Investigation of Creep Deformation in Copper-Chromium-Zirconium Alloy, a Candidate Heat Sink Material in Fusion Devices using Multiscale Experimental Methods
content: Heat sinks are a critical component inside fusion devices which would be subjected to high heat flux up to 15 MW/m2 and 300°C, hoop stresses and thermal mismatch stresses resulting to stress levels up to 200 MPa [1], [2]. Pure copper has excellent thermal conductivity, but its low mechanical strength at elevated temperatures makes it unsuitable for its use for fusion devices. CuCrZr alloys on the other hand exhibit the critical balance between thermal conductivity and structural reliability required for the longevity of heat sinks in fusion applications [3]. CuCrZr alloys have been studied under tensile loading and plastic deformation conditions; however, a notable gap persists in the availability of creep data at both macro and micro structural length scales [1]. Developing a macro and micro mechanistic understanding of the creep behaviour of CuCrZr alloys is critical for their application as heat sinks in such devices. This study investigates the strain localisation and grain deformation mechanisms during creep using multiscale characterisation techniques. The study aims to analyse the strain distribution across grains, focusing on the distributions of grain rotations measured using digital image correlation (DIC), maximum principal strains within the grains, strain components, inter and intra granular creep damage.
